author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both the veterinarian directory page and the machine-readable veterinarian list can be narrowed to a single specialty, matched on the whole name and disregarding letter case. Naming no specialty leaves either form unnarrowed.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are listed
given a narrowed directory page with more veterinarians than fit one page, when it is opened, then it is paged over the narrowed list, not the whole list
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable list is narrowed to it, then it carries only those veterinarians
given a specialty named in different letter case from the stored name, when either form is narrowed to it, then it matches
given a name matching only the beginning of a specialty's name, when either form is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is narrowed to it, then that form is returned successfully with no veterinarian in it
given an empty or all-spaces specialty name, when either form is narrowed to it, then it behaves as if no specialty were named
given no specialty named, when either form is requested, then every veterinarian is listed as before
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when either form is narrowed to any one of them, then that veterinarian is listed
REQ-VET-003: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable list is requested unnarrowed, then it carries every veterinarian with the specialties each holds
non_goals: free-text search for a veterinarian by name, or search for a pet or a visit (NG-9, narrowed but not withdrawn)
matching a specialty by prefix or substring
managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2)
narrowing by any attribute other than specialty
notes: Combined slice: covers REQ-VET-004 in full plus the one unfiltered-list criterion of REQ-VET-003 (the reinstated machine-readable surface), which is a single cycle on its own. Product-owner constraint on the external contract, decided and not open: both existing veterinarian-list URLs take an optional specialty query parameter; no new route is added, and the parameter name is fixed. The PRD keeps URLs and parameter names out by its own convention, so system-design owns recording that contract. Two follow-ups outside this agent's write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for 2026-08-07-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md, and system-design.md § Contracts still describes the machine-readable vet route as carrying no requirement.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Narrowing the veterinarian directory to one Specialty extends the vet feature package along its existing shape: a Spring Data derived finder on VetRepository, a request-bound parameter on the two VetController handlers, and the existing paged view. That much is the OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith precedent applied to a second feature package, and it needs no new package, layer, or type. Two things are genuinely new ground and are now recorded. First, the external contract (both published vet routes take one optional narrowing parameter rather than gaining narrowed twins) had no home, because the PRD keeps URLs out by convention and system-design.md keeps parameter literals out by its own rule; it is now fixed in docs/adr/2026-08-07-specialty-narrowing-on-existing-vet-routes.md, back-linked from system-design.md paragraph 'The veterinarian narrowing is an external contract' above the Contracts table. Second, this is the first time reader-supplied input can reach a cache key in this codebase: VetRepository's two reads carry @Cacheable("vets") and that cache declares no eviction and no size limit, so annotating a narrowed finder the same way would let any unauthenticated caller mint unbounded entries. Recorded as a decision in docs/adr/2026-08-07-reader-supplied-values-are-not-cache-keys.md and as a Threat Model row. REQ-VET-003's unfiltered machine-readable list already works in VetController.showResourcesVetList, so that criterion is a test-only addition.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived finders over the specialties association matching the whole name ignoring case - one returning Page<Vet> for the HTML directory, one returning Collection<Vet> for the machine-readable list. Neither carries @Cacheable; the two existing findAll methods keep theirs unchanged.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each bind an optional narrowing parameter, normalize it (strip, blank means absent), and choose between the unnarrowed and narrowed finder. No other handler or route changes.
vetList.html pagination links must carry the narrowing value, or paging past page one silently drops it. The controller adds the normalized value to the model for the links to read.
No schema, seed-data, or entity change. Specialty and the vet_specialties join table are used as they stand; Vet.getSpecialties keeps its name-sorted order, which PRD edge case 1 relies on.

patterns.description: derived finder with Pageable for a filtered, paged list - the shape the narrowed vet finder follows

request-value normalization in the controller: null becomes the broadest search, and the value is stripped. Blank-means-unnarrowed follows this precedent and is request adaptation, not a business rule, so it does not extend the controller deviation recorded in architecture-principles.md
the fixed external contract: parameter name, whole-name case-insensitive match, blank as absent, empty result as an ordinary 200
why the narrowed finders are uncached and must stay so

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed finder for symmetry with its neighbours - every other method on VetRepository carries @Cacheable("vets"), so this is the natural move. It makes unauthenticated caller text a key in a cache with no eviction and no size limit.
risks.mitigation: The narrowed finders carry no cache annotation. Recorded in the ADR and as a system-design.md Threat Model row so a reviewer meets it independently.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching delegated to the column type or collation, as owner search does. That is precisely how the PostgreSQL owner-search defect arose - the same query returns different results per vendor.
risks.mitigation: Express the comparison in the query (Spring Data IgnoreCase, or an explicit UPPER in JPQL) so it holds identically on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. system-design.md Persistence now records this as the fourth, vendor-independent route.

risks.risk: Pagination links built by string concatenation, as vetList.html does today, would neither carry nor encode the reader's value. An unencoded value in an href is a parameter-injection surface and drops the narrowing on the second page.
risks.mitigation: Build the links with Thymeleaf's URL builder so parameters are encoded; assert page-two narrowing in theVetDirectoryShouldPageOverTheNarrowedList.

risks.risk: Paging over an association join while Vet.specialties is EAGER can make Hibernate page in memory rather than in SQL.
risks.mitigation: Use a derived finder (a filter join, not a fetch join) so paging stays in SQL, exactly as the existing findAll(Pageable) does. The paging test over a narrowed list is the check.

risks.risk: Widening the slice into a visible filter control on the directory page. No acceptance criterion or test name calls for one, and any new user-facing wording pulls in REQ-LANG-002 - every string present in all eleven message bundles.
risks.mitigation: The narrowing is reached by the query parameter alone in this slice. Adding a control is a separate requirement.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Durable-memory writes made with this triage: two new ADRs (2026-08-07-specialty-narrowing-on-existing-vet-routes.md, 2026-08-07-reader-supplied-values-are-not-cache-keys.md); docs/adr/README.md index gains rows for both plus the missing row for 2026-08-07-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md (follow-up 1 from the prd-entry); docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for Vets, VetRepository, and VetController rewired to REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 with the external-contract paragraph added (follow-up 2), the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable route serves no requirement removed with a retirement note, a Persistence paragraph on vendor-independent case-insensitive matching, a Threat Model row for unbounded cache growth, and Open Question 5 narrowed to the unnarrowed reads. Giving Vets a requirement also settles a pre-existing inconsistency: the Contracts preamble says three kinds of contract carry an em-dash, and Vets was a fourth. Terminology check against docs/ubiquitous-language.md: Veterinarian and Specialty are the prose terms, Vet the accepted short form in code; 'narrow' is used rather than 'search' or 'filter' in prose, matching the PRD and NG-9 as amended.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the narrowing goes through Spring Data derived query methods (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and its Pageable overload) in VetRepository; the reader value is bound as a JPA parameter, no string-concatenated query text is introduced anywhere in the diff

Cache-key reasoning in docs/adr/2026-08-07-reader-supplied-values-are-not-cache-keys.md holds in the code as written: a sweep of @Cacheable across src/main/java returns only the two pre-existing VetRepository.findAll declarations; neither narrowed finder carries the annotation, so the eviction-free, size-unlimited 'vets' cache (system/CacheConfiguration.java) keeps a fixed, enumerable key space and the reader-supplied specialty never mints an entry

Cross-site scripting: the reader-supplied specialty reaches the page only inside th:href link expressions built with the Thymeleaf URL builder (@{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encodes the parameter value and then HTML-escapes the attribute; the value is rendered as text nowhere in vetList.html or any other template, and no th:utext, inlining, or escaping-disabling construct is added

Boundary normalization is at the boundary and fail-safe: VetController.narrowingSpecialty maps null, empty, and all-whitespace to null, and the null branch selects the unnarrowed finder, so no degenerate value reaches persistence and the absent-parameter case is spelled by omitting the parameter rather than by an empty one
Exposed surface is not widened: no new route is added; the change adds one optional query parameter to the two existing vet routes, both read-only GETs, and management-endpoint exposure is untouched
No secrets: the diff introduces no credential-shaped value; the only new literals are the specialty names in the test fixtures and the seeded specialty names in VetRepositoryTests
Mass assignment and identifier tampering are not in scope: the parameter binds to a String method argument, not to a command object, so no data binder or disallow list is involved
No path composition, no deserialization entry point, and no new error message carrying the reader value outward

Supply chain: build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, and gradle/ are unchanged in the change set, so no new or upgraded dependency enters and the four dependency checks in system-design.md have nothing to clear

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Eleven files but only one feature package: two prod Java files plus the vet-list template, two test files, and six documentation files (three new ADRs, PRD, system-design, ADR index). No sensitive paths, no schema or seed-data change, no shared type touched. The 53 hunks are inflated by the five pagination-link rewrites in vetList.html, each the same mechanical change. The widest real reach is documentary rather than executable: the PRD narrows non-goal NG-9, reinstates the machine-readable list as REQ-VET-003, and retires a Known Defects row in system-design.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every prod hunk for behavior the size would not predict and found none. Both handlers keep their existing signatures with an optional parameter, so unnarrowed callers hit the identical cached findAll paths; narrowingSpecialty strips and maps blank to null, and both call sites branch on that same null. The narrowed finders deliberately omit the cache annotation, which is the non-obvious decision here and it is the safe direction (reader input never becomes a key in an unbounded cache). The template ternary per link exists so an absent specialty omits the parameter rather than rendering it empty, and paging on the narrowed list would silently drop the filter without it. Derived-query risks I checked and cleared: the join on specialties yields at most one row per vet for a given name, so the Page count is a vet count, and the name-sorted specialty order is untouched. The value reaches the view only inside Thymeleaf URL builder syntax, so it is encoded and escaped, never echoed raw.

test_adequacy.note: The tests would fail against a broken implementation rather than restate it. The query semantics the code cannot control - whole-name matching, case insensitivity expressed in the query rather than delegated to collation - are pinned in a new DataJpaTest against real seeded H2, including the prefix non-match and a real two-specialty vet. The controller tests drop the Mockito stub for a hand-written in-memory repository doing real subList paging arithmetic, so the six-radiologist page-2 assertion exercises genuine offsets, and the rendered-content assertions check the actual page-1 link carries the escaped specialty parameter while the unnarrowed page carries no specialty parameter at all. Expected values are derived from the fixture rather than hard-coded.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three of the four dispatched reviewers approved with empty findings, but test-reviewer approved carrying one clarify finding addressed to system-design-expert: narrowingSpecialty is a new controller rule that testing-principles says should be answerable without booting the framework, and it is covered only indirectly through MockMvc. The reviewer marked it non-blocking and noted full branch coverage via the integration path, but the clarify was routed to another agent and no record answers it, so it merges as an open item rather than a settled one.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the triaged surface exactly. Every file changed appears in the design-block primary or supporting paths, and the REQ-VET-003 work that widens this beyond a pure filter was named in the original prd-entry as a deliberate combined slice, not picked up mid-flight. Zero consultations. The one design revision was bookkeeping - a superseding design-block adding three documentation paths the first record failed to list - and the single gate failure was that same autofix-audit path-coverage miss, with no production code implicated.

rationale: The code reads clean on every axis I could test by reading: contained, no surprising behavior, and tests that pin the query semantics against a real database. The one thing to look at is the test-reviewer unanswered clarify on narrowingSpecialty - a design question about unit-testability, not a defect. Read it, decide, merge.
